title: PUBLIC INFORMATION MEETING
full_story:
The City of Flora will have a public information meeting tonight at 4:15 pm.  The city is pursuing funding through the Illinois Transportation Enhancement Program (ITEP) for proposed sidewalk improvements to create safer pedestrian routes to local schools and the industrial park.

Residents, parents, property owners, employees, and community members are encouraged to attend, learn about the proposed project, ask questions, and share input.

The city needs the community to show their support for the project.  The meeting will be at 4:15 pm tonight, at Flora City Hall.

title: XENIA FIRE DEPARTMENT FISH FRY
full_story:
The Xenia Fire Department Fish Fry will be held on Saturday in the Xenia Village Park.  Lunch will be served starting at 11 am.  Along with fish sandwiches there will be hot dogs, fries and drinks.  There will also be vendors and a flavored lemonade stand.

The tractor pull and car show registration begin at Noon with admission $10 for adults and children 12 and under are free.  Pit passes are $15.  Car show awards will be at 3 pm.

There will be Carnival Games and prizes, inflatables and a petting zoo from Noon to 4 pm, with a $3 armband available good for unlimited activities.  There will be a silent auction at Noon.  The cake walk will be at 4 pm, bingo in the fire station starts at 5 pm and there will be live music from 7 to 10 pm.

All proceeds from the day go to the Xenia Volunteer Fire Department.

title: PARKER ARRESTED
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Division of Criminal Investigation Zone 8 Special Agents arrested 38-year-old Elizabeth “BethAnn’ Parker of Salem, for Forgery, a Class 3 Felony.

In January, the Department of Child and Family Services requested ISP investigate Parker after she allegedly provided falsified information indicating a juvenile suffered from an untrue illness.

After a thorough investigation, ISP Special Agents submitted their findings to the Marion County State’s Attorney’s Office.  On August 13th, the charge above was filed and ISP Special Agents took Parker into custody.

Parker appeared in Marion County Court Friday, she was released on pre-trial conditions pending her next court appearance on September 9th for a preliminary hearing.  The investigation started after a large fundraiser was held to help pay the medical expenses of the child who was not actually ill.

The charge is not evidence against the defendant, and the defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross announced an emergency blood shortage on July 13th.  Despite thousands of individuals stepping forward to help, the situation has escalated into a blood supply CRISIS.  For just the second time in history, the Red Cross has issued a national blood CRISIS.  Blood donations have fallen to a four-year summer low, worsening this summer’s emergency shortage.  A blood supply crisis is the most extreme blood shortage, posing a concerning risk to patient care.  Doctors will be forced to make difficult decisions about who receives blood transfusions and who will need to wait until more blood products become available.

The American Red Cross needs your help now so that hospital patients can continue to receive the transfusions they need.  All blood types are needed, but the situation is especially dire for type O blood as the Red Cross is now limiting distribution of these blood products to hospitals.  The type O positive blood supply has fallen below a one-day supply.  Blood donors are needed immediately to ensure hospitals have the blood they need for patients whose lives depend on transfusions.

To ease the shortage the American Red Cross has scheduled a Blood Drive for tomorrow, from 2 to 6 pm at the Mason Christian Church.  People donating at this drive will get a $20 Amazon Gift Card by email.

After Tuesday’s drive there will be a Blood Drive on Friday, August 31st at the Clay City High School from 1 to 5 pm sponsored by the Clay City High School Student Council.  By donating at this drive, donors are helping one or more graduating seniors earn a scholarship.

title: COVER CROP FIELD DAY
full_story:
The Wayne County Soil and Water Conservation District is hosting a Cover Crop Field Day tomorrow at 4 pm at the Greg Dickey Farm in Wayne City.

Speakers will be David Kleinschmidt from Progressive Agronomy Consulting LLC,Torey Colburn from American Farmland Trust, and Dave Severin from the Illinois House of Representative.  There will be in field demonstrations, comparisons and a Soil Pit.

There will also be a meal for participants catered by Randy’s Smokehouse in Wayne City.  The Cover Crop Field Day is sponsored by the American Farmland Trust, Peoples National Bank and Farm Credit.

The Greg Dickey farm is located at 981 County Road 530, Wayne City, for more information call 618-842-7602 Ext 3.

title: LOUISIANA MAN KILLED
full_story:
A 30-year-old Louisiana man was struck and killed by a car while walking in the passing lane of I-64 seven miles east of Mt. Vernon early Friday morning.

Jefferson County Coroner Roger Hayse pronounced Travon Thomas dead on the scene from blunt force trauma due to a motor vehicle crash.

Hayse says Thomas’ wife indicated her husband was walking back to Mt. Vernon after their car ran out of gas.  Hayse says Thomas was walking in the passing lane when he was hit by a mid-size car.

State Police have not released details on how the crash occurred or who was driving the car involved.  They say the crash is still under investigation.

The eastbound lanes of I-64 were closed for an investigation, and traffic was diverted onto Illinois Route 37 from shortly after the crash at 4:06 am Friday until approximately 8 am.

title: WAYNE COUNTY CROP TOUR SET
full_story:
The Wayne County Corn and Soybean Yield Tour is set for Monday, August 24th.  Gregg Barnard, Corn Grower President notes this will be the 43rd year for the tour.

Last year the soybean yield was 50.3 bushels per acre on 165,500 acres and a corn yield of 164.2 bushels per acre on 102,700 acres.

As in the past, eight teams will travel different routes, each checking at least 10 soybean and 10 corn fields for yield.  The teams will leave from JT’s in Wayne City at 7 am and meet back at the Wayne City Community Building at 11:30 am to compile the yield estimates.

Anyone interested in participating in the tour should contact the Wayne County Extension Office at 618-842-3702.  The crop tour is sponsored by Wayne County Corn Growers and University of Illinois Extension.  FNB Community Bank will provide lunch for participants.

title: COPPER THEFT LAW
full_story:
A new Illinois law aims to crack down on copper wire theft by restricting who can legally buy or sell the wire while also limiting how dealers can pay for it.

On July 31st, Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed House Bill 4943 into law, amending the state’s Recyclable Metal Purchase Registration Law in an effort to deter copper wire thefts.

The legislation, sponsored by Representative Jay Hoffman, makes it illegal to sell or purchase telecommunications wire unless the seller is an authorized agent or a licensed contractor of a public utility or telecommunications service.

The legislation also prohibits recyclable metal dealers from paying $100 or more in cash for telecommunications wire, copper tubing or copper wiring.

“We want to eliminate the financial incentives driving this behavior from bad actors,” said Hoffman.  “I appreciate the strong bipartisan support this legislation received, it’s important that we continue to look at ways to deter these thieves.”

Copper wire thefts have become a recurring problem around the St. Louis region in recent years.  Authorities say these crimes typically involve suspects stripping wire casings to access ultra-fine copper wiring, which can be burned to remove insulation and sold for scrap.

Illinois House Bill 4943 will officially take effect as law on January 1st.
